perspective:
Christian’s available information, from his subjective perspective:

- He knows he is Christian Mensah, a Black male police officer, and that Jonathan Balogun is his childhood best friend, more educated, and someone whose advice he often seeks.
- He felt anxious and suspicious that Jonathan was hiding something important, so he arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop and confronted him.
- He heard Jonathan admit he had been keeping something from him, that he was in some trouble, and that he hadn’t known how to tell him.
- He felt worried and empathetic, then offered to help Jonathan. Jonathan said the situation was complicated and he didn’t want to drag Christian into it, but that he could use support and resources to get out of a mess.
- He suspected the trouble might involve criminal activity and asked Jonathan directly. Jonathan said he couldn’t say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he had not done anything illegal himself.
- He told Jonathan he would look into the matter discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe Jonathan was being framed and set up. He told Jonathan he had leads and would gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- He later came to believe/know the real culprit was someone close to both him and Jonathan, a mutual trusted acquaintance. He told Jonathan he would confront them and bring them to justice.
- He heard Jonathan warn that this person is dangerous and express trust that Christian would do what is right.
- His own decisions and feelings include: deciding to help Jonathan, investigate discreetly, clear Jonathan’s name, gather evidence, and confront the culprit; feeling conflicted, concerned, determined, protective, betrayed, and resolute.
